HOPE FOR MND PATIENTS - EDARAVONE

By: Anna Teichert | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An intensive therapy, initially developed for stroke patients and approved by the FDA for MND, now gives hope to Andre Swartz and others suffering from the neurodegenerative disease with no cure

Unique Selling Point:
Andre Swartz, one of our countries leading and best known entertainers, was diagnosed in 2018 with MND, similar to Joost vd Westhuizen, while starring as Captain von Trapp in the theatre production of The Sound of Music.

Andre recently started using Edaravone, the generic of Radicava, that was initially developed for stroke patients. After three human trails on MND related diseases with a 30% improvement of degeneration, the FDA for the first time in twenty years approved the treatment in 2017 for MND patients.

The treatment is new in SA and not many people are aware of the option. Andre is positive and hopeful that the treatment will slow down the progression of the disease but has no illusions as to what might be lying ahead for him.

Summary:
The well-known entertainer Andre Swartz has recently started a therapy that he is hopeful will slow down the progression of MND that he was diagnosed with in 2018.

The therapy, Radicava/Endaravone was approved by the FDA in 2017; the first treatment that they have approved for MND diseases in twenty years. The therapy had proved in three human trials in China to have 30% effectiveness in the slowing down progression of this dibilitating, life-threatening disease with no cure.

Motor Neuron Disease is a neurodegenerative disease that affect the nerves (motor neurones) in the brain and spinal cord that tell your muscles what to do. With MND, messages from these nerves gradually stop reaching the muscles, leading them to weaken, stiffen and waste.

This treatment, that is still new in SA, is now giving hope to the many sufferers of MND.

Further information:
This proposal is for a story on Andre Swartz, who was diagnosed with MND, similar to Joost vd Westhuizen, and is undergoing a relatively new treatment approved by the FDA in 2017, that was initially developed for stroke patients.

Andre is well-known and loved by SA audiences for not only his music, but his performances in major theater productions such as the Pinocchio Pantomime, The Sound of Music etc. He will be a drawcard not only because of his fame, but also because he was diagnosed with MND and the whole country followed the progression of this life-threatening disease in Joost vd Westhuizen.

And now, the treatment that he recently started that is approved by the FDA, might bring hope to others suffering from the same disease!

According to André he is not angry or upset over the diagnosis and says he will deal with the cards that he was dealt. The actor, whose upper-body is mostly affected, is currently undergoing treatment to slow down the progression of the disease. It is similar to receiving chemotherapy via IV drip and Andre has opted for a mediport.

The therapy is taken intravenously daily for fourteen days, followed by fourteen days without the drug, then five days on treatment with two days off etc. The therapy is ongoing because the potential slowing of progression will only occur while the treatment is happening.

TREATMENT:
We will spend some time with Andre to see the effects that the disease have had on him so far, following his daily activities. According to him he first noticed a slight numbness on the left side of his tongue during his performance in the Pinocchio Pantomime in December 2017. His upper body is mostly affected so far, which might prove devastating for his performing career soon. In his introduction we will use footage of him on stage etc.

Presenter and two cameras for interviews with Andre, Neurologist in Jhb and the interviews in Cape Town with Dr Henning and Pieter Toerien. Should the female patient participate, interview could be done without the presenter.

STRUCTURE:
To incorporate the obvious mention of Joost, it will work well after an opening statement from Andre, something in the line of:

Andre: “I realize that I cannot get rid of this. What I thought was the future, is not there, what I thought would be tomorrow, is now uncertain. I know what the future might hold for me. I have to live with it”

Recap Joost: Previous CB/footage

Andre about symptoms and eventual diagnoses

Neurologist – What is MND, how complicated it is to diagnose, various types of MND’s etc

Pieter Toerien on Andre the person, his friend, performer, support during diagnostic period etc

Dr Henning as president of MND/ALS Ass SA on stats in SA, no cure, traditional options for treatment

Andre on the research, possible options he considered, advice etc and the choice eventually for the Edaravone therapy

Dr Henning on the history and development of Endavarone etc

Female patient on her treatment and how she is benefiting. This patient is not yet confirmed.

Neurologist on Andre’s treatment

Pieter Toerien on the treatment and Andre

Andre on side-effects etc

Dr Henning/Neorologist on side-effects and who would qualify for the therapy

Andre on the future, his positive attitude etc

Strong closing statement

Press Release:


André Schwartz – Hope for MND
Top Afrikaans artist and leading stage performer of ‘The Sound of Music’ and ‘Phantom of the Opera’, André Schwartz was diagnosed with motor neuron disease last year. Now he’s determined to give science a fighting chance as he embarks on a novel drug therapy that could slow the effects of the disease in its early stages. Edaravone, which is a disease-modifying treatment, previously used for stroke patients, has been approved by America’s FDA as a treatment for MND, for the first time in over two decades. It is expensive and its long-term effects have not been proven, but could this drug provide hope for patients?
Producer: Anna Teichert
Presenter: Claire Mawisa
Watch the trailer



Script:


HOPE FOR MND PATIENTS
Commission: 5406
AUDIO DUR
UPSOUND: Sound of Music Production & Phantom music video

V/O:
Renowned singer and performer Andre Schwartz is one of South Africa’s stage musical and Afrikaans popular music stars.

UPSOUND MUSIC

Andre was classically trained and has starred in one leading role after another.

UPSOUND: Lief vir alles hier

V/O:
And with his numerous Afrikaans hits, he’s built up a loyal following since he started performing at the age of fourteen.

Andre attributes his success to a number of factors.
ANDRE:
Discipline first and foremost. Understanding my craft. Wonderful loyal supporters and probably also doing various forms of the music genre and that’s kept me interested and hopefully an audience.

V/O:
From early on Andre cultivated versatility in his career.
3
ANDRE:
I am like a railway line. So two tracks, one being the Afrikaans music and the other the musicals. And I am the train. And I take a little bit of this and a little bit of that.

PIETER TOERIEN:
He is a star. So if you think about roles for Andre, you don’t think about anything other than the leading role.
V/O:
Theatre producer Pieter Toerien has brought several large musicals to the country and for him, Andre was born to lead.
7
PIETER TOERIEN:
Andre does not just sing a song. He interprets the song. He takes the words, he wraps his beautiful voice around it and gives it to us on a plate. He makes it easy.
V/O:
During The Sound of Music production in Cape Town last year, Andre received devastating news. He had Motor Neuron Disease, a diagnosis which would change the rest of his life.
10
LINK:
MND or motor neuron disease is a neurodegenerative disease that affect the nerves, or motor neurones in the brain and spinal cord that tell you muscles what to do. It is a life-shortening, progressive condition that still has no cure.
ANDRE SCHWARTZ:
My first question was “What is the way further now?” You know, do I… what happens from here? How long do I have? Because you know, most people only know the ugly side of MND. And it is quite a shock.
V/O:
The first symptoms appeared at the end of 2017, while Andre was doing vocal exercises.
5
ANDRE:
One of the vocal exercises is a ‘rrr’, it is a r sound. You role the tongue and I just suddenly found that only the right side of my tongue was working and the left side was completely lethargic.
V/O:
Initially Andre ignored it. Then in April last year during rehearsals he realised it wasn’t going away and he consulted a neurologist who confirmed the diagnosis.

He then did a lot of research.
8


2
ANDRE:
Google can be your worst, worst enemy! I went and I saw the worst and I put it in a box, and I thought “That is a long way away. I am not going to revisit this on a daily basis”. Otherwise I would not be able to put foot in front of the other.
V/O:
As a dear friend, Pieter was one of the first people that Andre turned to.
5
PIETER TOERIEN:
And you know his concern was for how I was going to take the news. There he was telling me unimaginable things about himself. And he was concerned about me! But that is Andre…
V/O:
There is no cure yet for MND, and the cause remains unknown, although scientists worldwide are working on ways to fight the disease.

For the last 24 years there’s only been one disease modifying treatment option… Riluzole.
8


5
LINK:
It was the only treatment available for MND. That is until Edaravone was FDA approved in 2017 for treatment of early stage patients.

ANDRE:
I decided to make an effort to trust science with this. I could tell my mom who is eighty-five, and a remarkable person, that I have got this but… there is now a treatment.
V/O:
Neurologist Dr Franslo Henning is the chairman of the Motor Neuron Disease Association of South Africa.
6
DR HENNING:
It is a medication that was used or tested initially for post-stroke patients in Japan. It is in a way an anti-oxidant.
V/O:
Henning says the FDA approved the compassionate use of Edaravone, based on evidence from clinical trials over only six months. Proper clinical trials generally range from twelve to eighteen months.
10
DR HENNING:
The reason for that is, we and the FDA realise that if you have ALS and are told that on average to expect three to four years, you don’t have the time to wait around for a well-controlled randomized study to be completed.
V/O:
The treatment is given via intravenous infusion and takes about sixty minutes for a full dose.
6
DR HENNING:
It is ten days per month that you get an infusion. The first treatment is for fourteen days, after that ten days for the rest of your life.
V/O:
Once infused into the bloodstream, Edaravone diffuses around the body, acting as free radical scavengers.
5
DR HENNING:
Edaravone aims to remove or decrease those oxygen radicals in the cell and thereby slow down the progression.
V/O:
A neuron consists of a cell body and an axon that runs all the way to the muscles they connect with.
7
DR HENNING:
If there is a disease process that affects the cell body, the axon will gradually die.
V/O:
The supply to the muscle is then non-existent and the ability of the brain to initiate and control muscle movement is lost.
8
LINK:
The clinical features or symptoms of neurodegenerative disorders depend on the particular regions of the nervous system that are affected.
V/O:
There are three types of MND that affect either upper- … or lower neurons… or both.

Andre doesn’t yet know which type he’s dealing with – he will find out when nerve conduction studies are performed on him in April.
7

8
ANDRE:
So then I will know medically conclusively. What I am feeling is that I am feeling fine.
V/O:
Because of the frequency of infusions, a port catheter is surgically placed into a main vein, usually in the upper chest area. This means Andre can take his treatment independently at home.
11
ANDRE:
I have weakness in my shoulders and some weakness in my hands. And my physio for my hands, is when I am getting a drip for an hour, I play piano.
V/O:
Edaravone is prescribed for only very early onset MND patients, if they have no breathing problems, which means only about seven percent of people diagnosed will be eligible to use it.

It has to be imported under a Section 21 Application form from the South African Health Products Regulatory Council and the costs are significant.
11


8
DR HENNING:
The costs in a way is irrelevant when you talk about these things because it is an individual decision to say: “I can justify, even if I am not sure. I am willing to take the risk.” And I think that is the argument that many people follow with for instance Edaravone because its safety profile is good. Except for the chronic venous access issue.

V/O:
Having a chronic venous access port is not without risks – like local infections, blockages in the catheter and even blood clots in the vein. A patient’s activity level may also drop significantly with prolonged treatments.

15

DR HENNING:
And I am not saying don’t take it because it is harmful. What I am saying is, there is some caution that needs to be applied and it is probably premature to say this is the new way to go.
V/O:
Andre is fighting back with healthy diet and lifestyle, a positive mindset and this novel drug.
6
ANDRE:
Because I now have something that is really trying to destroy me. But to let that alter the now would just be silly because then what is the point of having the now?
V/O:
Dr Henning says it often amazes him how MND patients may be shattered by the diagnosis, but regain hope.
6
DR HENNING:
That is why I find working with these patients so rewarding. They teach you about being human.
PIETER TOERIEN:
It is amazing how things work out. He was living in the city and he moved out to the farm. Almost in preparation for this. And he can change his lifestyle and rest more. I just hope he does, because all he seems to be doing is working!
ANDRE:
We don’t know what MND is going to do with it? We don’t know what it is going to do with my tongue that is my most vulnerable. I want to do what I love! So I am going to sing, you are going to see me everywhere. And I am just going to enjoy, you know. I love my space. Just… embrace it..

CLAIRE:
Live!

ANDRE:
Exactly. What we all should do, whether we have the disease or not! We must do it!



PROMO’S



Promo #1: 11 sec
V/O:

Diagnosed with motor neuron disease, celebrated classical musician Andre Schwartz is fighting back and using a recently FDA approved treatment to slow down the progression of the disease. (10)


Promo # 2: 11 sec
ANDRE:
I want to do what I love, so I am going to sing. You are going to see me everywhere. (5)

V/O:
Well-known singer, Andre Schwartz is fighting motor neuron disease with a newly approved treatment and a positive mindset. (6)



Promo #3: 11 sec
V/O:

Motor neuron disease is a terrifying degenerative disorder, but celebrated musician Andre Schwartz is determined to give science a chance, by using an FDA approved treatment to slow down its effects. (11)

nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 23 April 2019 Press Release: André Schwartz – Hope for MND Top Afrikaans artist and leading stage performer of ‘The Sound of Music’ and ‘Phantom of the Opera’, André Schwartz was diagnosed with motor neuron disease last year. Now he’s determined to give science a fighting chance as he embarks on a novel drug therapy that could slow the effects of the disease in its early stages. Edaravone, which is a disease-modifying treatment, previously used for stroke patients, has been approved by America’s FDA as a treatment for MND, for the first time in over two decades. It is expensive and its long-term effects have not been proven, but could this drug provide hope for patients? Producer: Anna Teichert Presenter: Claire Mawisa Watch the trailer Script: HOPE FOR MND PATIENTS Commission: 5406 AUDIO DUR UPSOUND: Sound of Music Production & Phantom music video V/O: Renowned singer and performer Andre Schwartz is one of South Africa’s stage musical and Afrikaans popular music stars. UPSOUND MUSIC Andre was classically trained and has starred in one leading role after another. UPSOUND: Lief vir alles hier V/O: And with his numerous Afrikaans hits, he’s built up a loyal following since he started performing at the age of fourteen. Andre attributes his success to a number of factors. ANDRE: Discipline first and foremost. Understanding my craft. Wonderful loyal supporters and probably also doing various forms of the music genre and that’s kept me interested and hopefully an audience. V/O: From early on Andre cultivated versatility in his career. 3 ANDRE: I am like a railway line. So two tracks, one being the Afrikaans music and the other the musicals. And I am the train. And I take a little bit of this and a little bit of that. PIETER TOERIEN: He is a star. So if you think about roles for Andre, you don’t think about anything other than the leading role. V/O: Theatre producer Pieter Toerien has brought several large musicals to the country and for him, Andre was born to lead. 7 PIETER TOERIEN: Andre does not just sing a song. He interprets the song. He takes the words, he wraps his beautiful voice around it and gives it to us on a plate. He makes it easy. V/O: During The Sound of Music production in Cape Town last year, Andre received devastating news. He had Motor Neuron Disease, a diagnosis which would change the rest of his life. 10 LINK: MND or motor neuron disease is a neurodegenerative disease that affect the nerves, or motor neurones in the brain and spinal cord that tell you muscles what to do. It is a life-shortening, progressive condition that still has no cure. ANDRE SCHWARTZ: My first question was “What is the way further now?” You know, do I… what happens from here? How long do I have? Because you know, most people only know the ugly side of MND. And it is quite a shock. V/O: The first symptoms appeared at the end of 2017, while Andre was doing vocal exercises. 5 ANDRE: One of the vocal exercises is a ‘rrr’, it is a r sound. You role the tongue and I just suddenly found that only the right side of my tongue was working and the left side was completely lethargic. V/O: Initially Andre ignored it. Then in April last year during rehearsals he realised it wasn’t going away and he consulted a neurologist who confirmed the diagnosis. He then did a lot of research. 8 2 ANDRE: Google can be your worst, worst enemy! I went and I saw the worst and I put it in a box, and I thought “That is a long way away. I am not going to revisit this on a daily basis”. Otherwise I would not be able to put foot in front of the other. V/O: As a dear friend, Pieter was one of the first people that Andre turned to. 5 PIETER TOERIEN: And you know his concern was for how I was going to take the news. There he was telling me unimaginable things about himself. And he was concerned about me! But that is Andre… V/O: There is no cure yet for MND, and the cause remains unknown, although scientists worldwide are working on ways to fight the disease. For the last 24 years there’s only been one disease modifying treatment option… Riluzole. 8 5 LINK: It was the only treatment available for MND. That is until Edaravone was FDA approved in 2017 for treatment of early stage patients. ANDRE: I decided to make an effort to trust science with this. I could tell my mom who is eighty-five, and a remarkable person, that I have got this but… there is now a treatment. V/O: Neurologist Dr Franslo Henning is the chairman of the Motor Neuron Disease Association of South Africa. 6 DR HENNING: It is a medication that was used or tested initially for post-stroke patients in Japan. It is in a way an anti-oxidant. V/O: Henning says the FDA approved the compassionate use of Edaravone, based on evidence from clinical trials over only six months. Proper clinical trials generally range from twelve to eighteen months. 10 DR HENNING: The reason for that is, we and the FDA realise that if you have ALS and are told that on average to expect three to four years, you don’t have the time to wait around for a well-controlled randomized study to be completed. V/O: The treatment is given via intravenous infusion and takes about sixty minutes for a full dose. 6 DR HENNING: It is ten days per month that you get an infusion. The first treatment is for fourteen days, after that ten days for the rest of your life. V/O: Once infused into the bloodstream, Edaravone diffuses around the body, acting as free radical scavengers. 5 DR HENNING: Edaravone aims to remove or decrease those oxygen radicals in the cell and thereby slow down the progression. V/O: A neuron consists of a cell body and an axon that runs all the way to the muscles they connect with. 7 DR HENNING: If there is a disease process that affects the cell body, the axon will gradually die. V/O: The supply to the muscle is then non-existent and the ability of the brain to initiate and control muscle movement is lost. 8 LINK: The clinical features or symptoms of neurodegenerative disorders depend on the particular regions of the nervous system that are affected. V/O: There are three types of MND that affect either upper- … or lower neurons… or both. Andre doesn’t yet know which type he’s dealing with – he will find out when nerve conduction studies are performed on him in April. 7 8 ANDRE: So then I will know medically conclusively. What I am feeling is that I am feeling fine. V/O: Because of the frequency of infusions, a port catheter is surgically placed into a main vein, usually in the upper chest area. This means Andre can take his treatment independently at home. 11 ANDRE: I have weakness in my shoulders and some weakness in my hands. And my physio for my hands, is when I am getting a drip for an hour, I play piano. V/O: Edaravone is prescribed for only very early onset MND patients, if they have no breathing problems, which means only about seven percent of people diagnosed will be eligible to use it. It has to be imported under a Section 21 Application form from the South African Health Products Regulatory Council and the costs are significant. 11 8 DR HENNING: The costs in a way is irrelevant when you talk about these things because it is an individual decision to say: “I can justify, even if I am not sure. I am willing to take the risk.” And I think that is the argument that many people follow with for instance Edaravone because its safety profile is good. Except for the chronic venous access issue. V/O: Having a chronic venous access port is not without risks – like local infections, blockages in the catheter and even blood clots in the vein. A patient’s activity level may also drop significantly with prolonged treatments. 15 DR HENNING: And I am not saying don’t take it because it is harmful. What I am saying is, there is some caution that needs to be applied and it is probably premature to say this is the new way to go. V/O: Andre is fighting back with healthy diet and lifestyle, a positive mindset and this novel drug. 6 ANDRE: Because I now have something that is really trying to destroy me. But to let that alter the now would just be silly because then what is the point of having the now? V/O: Dr Henning says it often amazes him how MND patients may be shattered by the diagnosis, but regain hope. 6 DR HENNING: That is why I find working with these patients so rewarding. They teach you about being human. PIETER TOERIEN: It is amazing how things work out. He was living in the city and he moved out to the farm. Almost in preparation for this. And he can change his lifestyle and rest more. I just hope he does, because all he seems to be doing is working! ANDRE: We don’t know what MND is going to do with it? We don’t know what it is going to do with my tongue that is my most vulnerable. I want to do what I love! So I am going to sing, you are going to see me everywhere. And I am just going to enjoy, you know. I love my space. Just… embrace it.. CLAIRE: Live! ANDRE: Exactly. What we all should do, whether we have the disease or not! We must do it! (10) Promo # 2: 11 sec ANDRE: I want to do what I love, so I am going to sing. You are going to see me everywhere. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): An intensive therapy, initially developed for stroke patients and approved by the FDA for MND, now gives hope to Andre Swartz and others suffering from the neurodegenerative disease with no cure
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Andre Swartz, one of our countries leading and best known entertainers, was diagnosed in 2018 with MND, similar to Joost vd Westhuizen, while starring as Captain von Trapp in the theatre production of The Sound of Music. Andre recently started using Edaravone, the generic of Radicava, that was initially developed for stroke patients. After three human trails on MND related diseases with a 30% improvement of degeneration, the FDA for the first time in twenty years approved the treatment in 2017 for MND patients. The treatment is new in SA and not many people are aware of the option. Andre is positive and hopeful that the treatment will slow down the progression of the disease but has no illusions as to what might be lying ahead for him.
metadata.Summary: The well-known entertainer Andre Swartz has recently started a therapy that he is hopeful will slow down the progression of MND that he was diagnosed with in 2018. The therapy, Radicava/Endaravone was approved by the FDA in 2017; the first treatment that they have approved for MND diseases in twenty years. The therapy had proved in three human trials in China to have 30% effectiveness in the slowing down progression of this dibilitating, life-threatening disease with no cure. Motor Neuron Disease is a neurodegenerative disease that affect the nerves (motor neurones) in the brain and spinal cord that tell your muscles what to do. With MND, messages from these nerves gradually stop reaching the muscles, leading them to weaken, stiffen and waste. This treatment, that is still new in SA, is now giving hope to the many sufferers of MND.
metadata.Further information: This proposal is for a story on Andre Swartz, who was diagnosed with MND, similar to Joost vd Westhuizen, and is undergoing a relatively new treatment approved by the FDA in 2017, that was initially developed for stroke patients. Andre is well-known and loved by SA audiences for not only his music, but his performances in major theater productions such as the Pinocchio Pantomime, The Sound of Music etc. He will be a drawcard not only because of his fame, but also because he was diagnosed with MND and the whole country followed the progression of this life-threatening disease in Joost vd Westhuizen. And now, the treatment that he recently started that is approved by the FDA, might bring hope to others suffering from the same disease! According to André he is not angry or upset over the diagnosis and says he will deal with the cards that he was dealt. The actor, whose upper-body is mostly affected, is currently undergoing treatment to slow down the progression of the disease. It is similar to receiving chemotherapy via IV drip and Andre has opted for a mediport. The therapy is taken intravenously daily for fourteen days, followed by fourteen days without the drug, then five days on treatment with two days off etc. The therapy is ongoing because the potential slowing of progression will only occur while the treatment is happening. TREATMENT: We will spend some time with Andre to see the effects that the disease have had on him so far, following his daily activities. According to him he first noticed a slight numbness on the left side of his tongue during his performance in the Pinocchio Pantomime in December 2017. His upper body is mostly affected so far, which might prove devastating for his performing career soon. In his introduction we will use footage of him on stage etc. Presenter and two cameras for interviews with Andre, Neurologist in Jhb and the interviews in Cape Town with Dr Henning and Pieter Toerien. Should the female patient participate, interview could be done without the presenter. STRUCTURE: To incorporate the obvious mention of Joost, it will work well after an opening statement from Andre, something in the line of: Andre: “I realize that I cannot get rid of this. What I thought was the future, is not there, what I thought would be tomorrow, is now uncertain. I know what the future might hold for me. I have to live with it” Recap Joost: Previous CB/footage Andre about symptoms and eventual diagnoses Neurologist – What is MND, how complicated it is to diagnose, various types of MND’s etc Pieter Toerien on Andre the person, his friend, performer, support during diagnostic period etc Dr Henning as president of MND/ALS Ass SA on stats in SA, no cure, traditional options for treatment Andre on the research, possible options he considered, advice etc and the choice eventually for the Edaravone therapy Dr Henning on the history and development of Endavarone etc Female patient on her treatment and how she is benefiting. This patient is not yet confirmed. Neurologist on Andre’s treatment Pieter Toerien on the treatment and Andre Andre on side-effects etc Dr Henning/Neorologist on side-effects and who would qualify for the therapy Andre on the future, his positive attitude etc Strong closing statement
